extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy of science / scientists interested in the classification and methodology of the sciences
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and evaluative criteria for dividing knowledge into Abstract, Physical, and Biological sciences, and for distinguishing subfields (e.g., precise vs synoptic, descriptive vs metrical). Explains what counts as a precise science, a synoptic science, and cross-linking disciplines like applied mathematics and biophysics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract Science — modes of discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract Science (Logic and Pure Mathematics) deals with conceptual modes of discrimination; concepts are narrowly defined and free from the infinite complexity of perception, enabling reasoning with great preciseness and results absolutely valid for all that falls under their definitions and axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract Science embraces logic and pure mathematics; because its concepts are narrowly defined, conclusions are exact within definitions and axioms. This grounds it being called the Exact Sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive (Geometry of Position) vs Metrical Geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: One may treat spatial relations solely by relative positions of points, lines and surfaces without quantitative measurements (Descriptive Geometry or Geometry of Position, including Perspective Geometry), or treat the quantitative/measuring side concerned with size (Metrical Geometry, Trigonometry, Mensuration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish whether a spatial science is concerned with qualitative localization (descriptive) or quantitative measurement (metrical); both are valid subdivisions with different aims and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory of Observation and Description for qualitative change
rubrics_metrics.description: When changes are not measured quantitatively but only described qualitatively, we require a theory by aid of which we may accurately observe and describe such changes — i.e., a scientific theory of observation and description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific training is needed not only to know what is essential to observe in organic phenomena, but how observations should be described; treatises on Logic touch this but fuller treatment is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinematics (Geometry of Motion) as quantitative change in position
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantitative side of change allowing consideration of motion of conceptual bodies without reference to special structures is termed Kinematics or the Geometry of Motion; foundational for describing constrained motion and machine construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of its fundamental importance, Kinematics underpins many applied constructions and has advanced theoretically and practically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Precise Physical Sciences — reduced to ideal motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Precise Physical Sciences are those where phenomena have been conceptualized by aid of ideal particles with ideal motions (reduced to ideal motions), enabling brief formulae/laws (e.g., gravitation) that accurately resume facts and permit precise prediction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a field admits a conceptual mechanism of elementary corpuscles and simple laws describing changes, it is classed as Precise (e.g., Astronomy, parts of Theoretical Chemistry, Spectrum Analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Synoptic Physical Sciences — not yet reduced to ideal motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Synoptic Physical Sciences are those not yet completely reduced to ideal motions; they may offer rational classification of facts but lack a conceptual mechanism or simple formulae enabling precise prediction (e.g., Meteorology, parts of Chemistry, Geology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synoptic sciences often embrace large classifications of facts that are in process of being resumed into simple laws; many are 'precise in the making.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for rational classification in Synoptic Physical Sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Synoptic Physical Sciences we demand a rational classification of physical phenomena which have not been conceptualized by simple formulae of motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such classification is particularly needed where many elementary bodies would be required for synthesis; it helps progress toward precise conceptual descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision of Physical Sciences by corpuscle scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical sciences can be classified by the conceptual corpuscle used: Molar Physics (motion of bodies; mechanics, planetary, lunar theory), Molecular Physics (relative motion of molecules; elasticity, viscosity, sound, crystallography, hydromechanics), Atomic Physics (motions of atoms; theoretical chemistry, spectrum analysis), and Physics of the Ether (relative motions of ether-elements; radiation, light, heat, electricity, magnetism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the level of conceptual particles (mole, molecule, atom, ether-elements) as a basis for subdividing precise physical sciences and associating topics with appropriate scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological Sciences subdivision: space (localization) vs time (growth/change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological sciences are fruitfully subdivided into those dealing with space/localization (distribution of living forms, ecology, natural history) and those dealing with time/growth or sequence (recurring = biology in narrower sense; non-recurring = history, evolution of species/man).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subdivision clarifies branches such as botany/zoology, morphology, embryology, physiology, psychology, sociology, and historical treatments like paleontology and anthropology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: recurring vs non-recurring growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurring changes (treated by biology narrowly) and non-recurring changes (treated as history) are practical classifications of perceptual experience rather than metaphysical claims; e.g., evolution of species may be treated as non-recurring in human experience but could be recurring cosmically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recurring/non-recurring to separate biological topics: morphology/growth/reproduction vs historical evolution and human institutional history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Biology into morphology, heredity/embryology, and functions/actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Biology divides into (1) form and structure (morphology, histology, anatomy), (2) growth and reproduction (theory of sex, heredity, embryology), and (3) functions and actions (physiology for physical side; psychology for mental side; sociology for group behavior and social institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tripartite scheme helps allocate biological topics and indicates methodological differences (physical description vs mental/functional description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applied Mathematics and Biophysics as cross-links
rubrics_metrics.description: Applied Mathematics links Abstract Science to the Physical Sciences by analyzing inorganic phenomena via ideal elementary motions; Biophysics (Etiology) attempts to apply laws of inorganic phenomena to biological facts, linking Physical and Biological Sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize these fields as bridges: applied mathematics connects abstract kinematics to molar/molecular descriptions; biophysics seeks to show biological facts as particular cases of general physical laws (e.g., conservation of energy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification is provisional and dependent on scientific development
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual's classification has temporary value: the position of a science relative to others changes with its development (e.g., synoptic fields may become precise), and the best form of classification may be a branching tree but must account for interdependence among sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt flexible classifications acknowledging historical and developmental shifts; use branching tree models (Bacon) while allowing interdependence (Comte) and abstract/concrete distinction (Spencer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific method requirement: 'dare to be ignorant' and avoid metaphysical shortcuts
rubrics_metrics.description: When science lacks descriptive formulae (e.g., genesis of life), the duty is to avoid superstition or metaphysics and to accept ignorance until adequate classification and description arise ('we must dare to be ignorant').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological humility and refusal to substitute metaphysical guesses for empirical classification and conceptual description are presented as scientific virtues.
